  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

`read_agricultural_commodities()` reads two related but distinct workbook
families: medium-term Agricultural Commodities outlooks and Agricultural
Commodity Statistics (ACS). This article uses the package's small,
package-owned synthetic workbooks. They preserve workbook shapes and marker
tokens for deterministic parser examples; their values are not official
ABARES data.

## Setup and offline fixtures

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE
)

library(readagau)

fixture <- function(...) {
  path <- system.file("fixtures", ..., package = "readagau")
  stopifnot(nzchar(path))
  path
}

march_path <- fixture("workbooks", "ac-march-outlook.xlsx")
june_path <- fixture("workbooks", "ac-june-outlook.xlsx")
statistics_path <- fixture("workbooks", "commodity-statistics.xlsx")
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("readagau-ac-vignette-", Sys.getpid()))
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

Passing named local paths makes the dataset role explicit and keeps all
examples offline. The reader still records a local checksum identity and the
physical source asset in every returned row.

## Compare outlook profiles

March and non-March outlooks have different admitted sheet layouts. Let the
parser identify the profile from sheet structure rather than relying on a
sheet position or a hand-written column offset.

```{r outlook-profiles}
march <- read_agricultural_commodities(
  c(outlook = march_path),
  datasets = "outlook",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
june <- read_agricultural_commodities(
  c(outlook = june_path),
  datasets = "outlook",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

stopifnot(
  inherits(march, "agricultural_commodities_data"),
  inherits(june, "agricultural_commodities_data"),
  all(march$dataset == "commodities_outlook"),
  all(june$dataset == "commodities_outlook")
)

data.frame(
  profile = c("March outlook", "non-March outlook"),
  observations = c(nrow(march), nrow(june)),
  tables = c(length(unique(march$table_id)), length(unique(june$table_id))),
  release_id = c(unique(march$release_id), unique(june$release_id))
)
```

The shared observation contract retains target period, status, source sheet,
semantic table, unit, and provenance. The nested heading dimensions used by
outlook tables are explicit fields rather than display-only text:

```{r outlook-contract}
knitr::kable(utils::head(
  march[c(
    "source_asset", "source_sheet", "table_id", "table_title", "sector",
    "commodity", "concept", "period", "period_basis", "period_status",
    "unit", "currency", "price_basis", "value", "raw_value"
  )],
  8L
))
```

An unsuffixed source period remains `published-unclassified`; suffixes retain
the source's estimate, forecast, or projection status. Do not treat the
status as a guess based on the position of a year in a row.

## Read ACS statistics and preserve missing markers

ACS has its own table family. Select it with `datasets = "statistics"` and
inspect the controlled `missing_reason` field when a cell is not numeric.
Missing, suppressed, confidential, unavailable, and provider-specific `NA`
markers remain numeric `NA`; they are never silently converted to zero.

```{r acs-statistics}
acs <- read_agricultural_commodities(
  c(statistics = statistics_path),
  datasets = "statistics",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
acs_validation <- validate_agau_release(acs)
stopifnot(
  inherits(acs, "agricultural_commodities_data"),
  isTRUE(acs_validation$valid),
  all(grepl("^acs_table_", acs$table_id))
)

data.frame(
  class = class(acs)[1L],
  observations = nrow(acs),
  tables = length(unique(acs$table_id)),
  valid = acs_validation$valid,
  missing_cells = sum(!is.na(acs$missing_reason))
)
```

```{r acs-missing-preview}
missing <- acs[!is.na(acs$missing_reason), c(
  "table_id", "source_sheet", "commodity", "concept", "period",
  "raw_value", "value", "missing_reason"
), drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(utils::head(missing, 8L))
```

If a source contains no missing markers, `missing` is an empty table and the
contract still holds. Use `raw_value` and `missing_reason` together when
auditing a source or explaining why a numeric value is absent.

## Reported and canonical views

`view = "reported"` is the source-faithful view. `view = "canonical"` applies
the versioned precedence policy to semantically equivalent observations and
marks the retained rows as canonical. For Agricultural Commodities, outlook
rows take precedence for estimates and forecasts, while statistics rows are
preferred for historical observations when their identities are equivalent.
The policy does not merge distinct markets, currencies, units, methods, or
period bases.

```{r ac-views}
march_canonical <- read_agricultural_commodities(
  c(outlook = march_path),
  datasets = "outlook",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
stopifnot(
  inherits(march_canonical, "agricultural_commodities_data"),
  all(march_canonical$record_role == "canonical")
)

data.frame(
  view = c("reported", "canonical"),
  observations = c(nrow(march), nrow(march_canonical)),
  canonical_rows = c(
    sum(march$record_role == "canonical"),
    sum(march_canonical$record_role == "canonical")
  )
)
```

To compare two releases, prefer exact release IDs and retain the source
metadata. The vintage helpers compare semantic keys rather than row numbers;
see `vignette("comparing-revisions-and-errors")` for revision and forecast
error operations.

## Table and series metadata

Use the source catalogue when you need to explain which table families are
admitted. It is metadata and does not contain a claim that the synthetic
fixtures are official data.

```{r acs-catalogue}
catalogue <- agau_source_catalog()
acs_catalogue <- catalogue[
  catalogue$product == "agricultural_commodities" &
    catalogue$dataset == "commodity_statistics" &
    grepl("^acs_table_", catalogue$table_id),
  c("table_id", "source_label", "semantic_family", "parser_family",
    "admission_status"),
  drop = FALSE
]
knitr::kable(utils::head(acs_catalogue, 8L))
```

## Online use and provenance

The examples above deliberately use local files. For a live workflow, select
an exact supported release from `list_agau_releases()` and pass that release ID
to the reader. A missing exact asset may be downloaded into the managed
`tools::R_user_dir()` cache; a complete local path or exact cache hit can be
replayed offline. No credentials are required for the public source pages,
but network availability, upstream layout changes, and source-data terms are
outside the package's control.

When publishing derived results, retain `release_id`, `release_date`,
`source_url`, `sha256`, `parser_version`, and the relevant attribution fields.
Package code and package-owned synthetic fixtures: MIT, copyright Chartwell Macro.
Source data, logos, government marks, and third-party material remain subject
to their own terms.
